items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: features Arnold Ross, piano, Harry Babasin, cello, Joe Comfort, bass and Alvin Stoller drums.

ctx.x: Al was living on 52nd street not far from the pier, which I think was at 42nd street and Riverside Drive. Lily and I were in a hotel at 25th street and 7th Avenue. We had packed our baggage and had to go and get them with a taxi. There was no need for Lily to go to the hotel with me, so Oscar came along and the rest of the party went to the pier with Lily where

we all met to say farewell. Oscar gave me two of his recordings with his autograph, which are priceless to me. One was an L.P. on Debut Records called "The new Oscar Pettiford Sextet" and features the man himself with Phil Urso, tenor, Julius Watkins, french horn, Walter Bishop, piano, Charles Mingus, bass and Percy Brice, drums. Oscar played cello. The other record was a 45 rpm on Imperial records and has Oscar still playing cello and features Arnold Ross, piano, Harry Babasin, cello, Joe Comfort, bass and Alvin…

We were on the Flandre, another ship of the French line, very nice but much smaller than the Liberte. It left the pier around 11 o'clock the 3rd of June and after we waved to our friends until we could no longer see them. Lily couldn't take it any longer and went to our cabin to rest her tired body. I stayed up to see the statue of Liberty because I wanted to film it and then I hit the hay for the rest of the afternoon.
